This section details six project case studies to identify potential drivers and contextual factors that may influence successful cost allocation and project outcomes. 3.1 Case Study Selection The case studies selected for investigation are designed to capture diverse factors that may influence the outcome of a cost allocation agreement. These include the complexity of the cost allocation method, the regional flexibility with which costs are assigned, the portfolio of the transmission project(s), and the existence of a state project champion. In addition, the case studies include a range of different RTOs/ISOs, including single-state and multistate systems. Figure 4. Summary of project case studies classified by factors that may influence the cost allocation outcome Figure 4 classifies our selected case studies according to these factors. • Method complexity: The complexity of the cost allocation method refers to the input data, modeling, and calculations required to identify cost responsibility. Methods that require production cost or power flow modeling are considered more “complex.” We consider “simple” cost allocation methods to be those that do not require economic- or reliability- based power system modeling. This includes variations of the load ratio share, whereby costs are allocated in proportion to electricity load. 12 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. • Regional flexibility: The regional flexibility refers to the ability to assign costs differently within a given region.
